correctness.rationale: Core facts and date-attribution logic are mostly sound, but RLS inconsistencies and a few missing/uneven constraints (e.g., Cronometer onyx_* triggers, missing FK in prod) leave room for incorrect states.

robustness.rationale: Good use of constraints, CHECKs, and helper views; ADR-0001 trigger ladder is thorough, though scattered per-table triggers create drift risk.

scalability.rationale: Indexes generally align with query patterns and volumes are modest; a few missing/duplicate indexes and a heavy “god view” could be tuned but won’t block 3–5× growth.

idiomaticness.rationale: Largely idiomatic Postgres (partial indexes, DEFERRABLE FKs, vector HNSW), marred by earlier public-targeted RLS policies and some duplicated trigger logic.

response.summary:
Overall this schema is in good shape for a single-user analytics stack: behavioral-day attribution is enforced by database triggers rather than application code; key WHOOP and Spotify relationships are now FK-enforced; and the HRV predictions table and views have been hardened with a surrogate PK and a clear tiebreak. The heavy-lift daily matrix switched to a behavioral spine and extracted dedup logic into helper views, improving clarity and testability.

Where it wobbles is consistency and enforcement. Production (as captured 2026-05-25) still shows RLS policies granting ALL to public on some tables and, more seriously, a pre-lockdown state where authenticated could write habit tables; the lockdown SQL in this bundle closes that, but it must be applied. Referential integrity remains selective in production (e.g., no FK from habit_journal.question to habit_name_map.habit_name), despite an included migration to add it. Cronometer tables were introduced without the ADR-0001 set_onyx_dates triggers, relying on the importer to populate onyx_* — that’s brittle and inconsistent with the rest of the design.

The riskiest choices are: (1) RLS policy drift and past overbroad grants; (2) absent FK(s) that should be present to prevent silent orphaning; (3) wide views that accumulate complexity. If I could only fix three things: (1) apply the security_lockdown and rls_policies migrations to normalize RLS (service_role-only writes); (2) add and validate the habit_journal.question → habit_name_map.habit_name FK in production; (3) add Cronometer set_onyx_dates triggers so the onyx_* invariants are enforced at write-time, not by ETL convention. Secondary cleanups: drop duplicate indexes, ensure the HRV tiebreak index exists, and remove garmin_daily_summary from the behavioral spine once consumers are migrated.

findings.title: Pre-lockdown RLS allowed habit writes via authenticated role
findings.description: Before the lockdown migration, habit_journal and habit_name_map had FOR ALL policies to authenticated plus table-level write grants, enabling public-key writes. This is a direct integrity and security risk if not already applied in prod.
findings.evidence: sql/security_lockdown_2026_06_06.sql comments: 'habit_journal / habit_name_map had ... FOR ALL to authenticated + anon/authenticated table-level write grants, so the public key could INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE...'.
findings.recommendation: Ensure the lockdown migration is applied: scope service_full_access to service_role only and revoke anon/authenticated writes on both tables as in sql/security_lockdown_2026_06_06.sql.

findings.title: Missing FK: habit_journal.question → habit_name_map.habit_name (prod)
findings.description: Production snapshot lists only six FKs and explicitly calls out this relationship as absent; the migration to add the FK exists but appears not applied. Without the FK, typos/renames can orphan rows.
findings.evidence: SCHEMA_DDL.md: 'Notably absent foreign keys — habit_journal.question ↔ habit_name_map.name'; migration present in sql/audit_re_2026_05_26_habit_journal_question_fk.sql.
findings.recommendation: Apply sql/audit_re_2026_05_26_habit_journal_question_fk.sql (adds UNIQUE on habit_name and FK with ON UPDATE CASCADE, ON DELETE RESTRICT). Validate no orphans exist first.

findings.title: Cronometer tables lack set_onyx_dates triggers
findings.description: New Cronometer tables define onyx_* columns but no BEFORE triggers to populate them, diverging from ADR-0001’s trigger-enforced invariant and risking drift if ETL forgets to set them.
findings.evidence: cronometer_schema.sql creates onyx_* columns and indexes but no pds.set_onyx_dates_* triggers; SCHEMA_DDL lists 11 set_onyx_dates triggers for other sources, not Cronometer.
findings.recommendation: Add BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE triggers: for daily, set all onyx_* = calendar_date; for servings, call derive_onyx_dates(event_time) when present else default to calendar_date with explicit tz_source.

findings.title: Inconsistent RLS: service_full_access granted TO public on some tables
findings.description: Several service_full_access policies target the public role instead of service_role, widening the trust boundary and creating future risk if table grants change.
findings.recommendation: Normalize to service_role-only per sql/rls_policies.sql; drop any public-targeted write policies.

findings.title: Redundant single-column indexes that duplicate PKs
findings.description: Indexes like idx_mfp_nutrition_date, idx_weight_log_date, and whoop_journal(cycle_date) duplicate the PK’s leading column and add maintenance/plan noise.
findings.evidence: SCHEMA_DDL.md flags 'duplicate?' next to these indexes.
findings.recommendation: Drop the redundant indexes; keep only the PK or a truly different composite/partial index. Use sql/audit_re_2026_05_26_drop_redundant_indexes.sql as a pattern.

findings.title: garmin_activity_laps has redundant (activity_id, lap_index) index
findings.description: A separate index on (activity_id, lap_index) duplicates the leftmost prefix of the UNIQUE (activity_id, lap_index, ts) index and is likely unnecessary.
findings.evidence: SCHEMA_DDL.md shows UNIQUE(activity_id, lap_index, ts) and a separate idx(activity_id, lap_index).
findings.recommendation: Drop the two-column index unless you can show a measurable plan benefit; the UNIQUE index supports scans on the leftmost prefix.

findings.title: Behavioral-spine view still unions garmin_daily_summary.calendar_date
findings.description: The behavioral matrix spine unions GDS calendar_date (watch-local), which can diverge from onyx_behavioral_date on travel days. A comment notes a pending removal, but prod state suggests it’s still included.
findings.evidence: sql/daily_health_matrix_behavioral_main_session.sql NOTE: migration to remove GDS from UNION is pending; current UNION includes garmin_daily_summary.calendar_date.
findings.recommendation: Remove garmin_daily_summary from the UNION and regenerate the spine from behavioral onyx_* dates only; backfill any gaps via other sources.

findings.title: Missing/uncertain HRV tiebreak index may force full scans
findings.description: The view orders by a CASE tiebreak; production index list only shows idx(input_data_hash). Without idx_hrv_predictions_tiebreak, DISTINCT ON queries may scan/sort the whole table.
findings.evidence: SCHEMA_DDL.md index list omits the composite tiebreak index; sql/hrv_predictions_latest.sql creates it explicitly.
findings.recommendation: Ensure sql/hrv_predictions_latest.sql has been applied and idx_hrv_predictions_tiebreak exists; ANALYZE the table after creation.

findings.title: Hot-path partial/composite indexes not present in prod snapshot
findings.description: Indexes tailored to frequent filters (WHOOP score_state='SCORED', non-nap sleep, Garmin sleep best-of-day, Spotify featurized-join) aren’t listed in production.
findings.evidence: SCHEMA_DDL.md index inventory lacks idx_whoop_recovery_cycle_scored, idx_whoop_sleep_cycle_scored_main, idx_garmin_sleep_behavioral_score, idx_spotify_tracks_featurized.
findings.recommendation: Apply sql/audit_re_2026_05_26_covering_partial_indexes.sql to tighten join and aggregate performance.

findings.title: Duplication in 11+ set_onyx_dates triggers invites drift
findings.description: Each source table has a bespoke trigger function that mirrors the same ladder; fixes must be repeated across many functions, risking skew over time.
findings.evidence: SCHEMA_DDL.md: '11 of these' set_onyx_dates_* functions; ADR-0001 edits had to be repeated.
findings.recommendation: Refactor to a single generic trigger function with TG_ARGs (instant column, provenance) or a small set of shared helpers to centralize logic and reduce maintenance.

findings.title: Legacy daily_health_matrix likely ready for deprecation
findings.description: Two parallel matrix views increase maintenance surface and confusion; the behavioral one is canonical and already powers downstream methods.
findings.evidence: CONTEXT.md: legacy retained for migration; SCHEMA_DDL.md lists both; behavioral view has helper refactors and richer semantics.
findings.recommendation: Migrate remaining consumers and deprecate/drop the legacy view; keep a frozen snapshot if historical A/B comparisons are still needed.

findings.title: Several tables lack explicit service_role write policies in prod
findings.description: Production notes tables with only anon_read and no service policy, relying on service-role bypass. This is brittle and non-idiomatic.
findings.evidence: SCHEMA_DDL.md: 'A few tables have RLS enabled with anon_read but no service_* policy... rely on the service-role’s bypass-RLS privilege.'
findings.recommendation: Apply sql/rls_policies.sql to add explicit FOR ALL TO service_role policies consistently across all writeable tables.

things_done_well.title: WHOOP cycle hub and Spotify FKs with sensible ON DELETE actions
things_done_well.why_it_matters: Enforcing recovery/sleep→cycle and plays→track/artist at write-time prevents silent join-corruption and preserves ETL idempotency; DEFERRABLE aids ingest ordering.

things_done_well.title: Behavioral-day attribution enforced in the database
things_done_well.why_it_matters: Putting the TZ ladder and -6h boundary in triggers removes application ambiguity and catches attribution mistakes early, which is critical for downstream analytics.

things_done_well.title: hrv_predictions hardened with surrogate PK and tiebreak index
things_done_well.why_it_matters: Allows multiple versions per (date,model,horizon) while keeping latest selection deterministic and efficient; avoids silent overwrites.

things_done_well.title: Supplement JSONB + per-compound rollup with unit normalization
things_done_well.why_it_matters: Combines flexibility (JSONB) with analytical clarity (UNII-based rollups, mg normalization) and surfaces unmapped units to avoid silent data loss.

things_done_well.title: Helper views for per-day dedup in behavioral matrix
things_done_well.why_it_matters: Moving LATERAL+LIMIT patterns into reusable views clarifies intent, reduces duplication, and makes testing per-source selection logic tractable.

things_done_well.title: Vector HNSW index on journal embeddings
things_done_well.why_it_matters: Using the right operator class and index type enables fast semantic search without custom infrastructure.

questions_for_followup: Have sql/security_lockdown_2026_06_06.sql and sql/rls_policies.sql been applied to production? If not, is there any reason to defer?
Was sql/audit_re_2026_05_26_habit_journal_question_fk.sql applied (and validated) in prod? If blocked, what data issue prevents it?
Do the Cronometer importers currently populate onyx_* consistently, or should we add the recommended set_onyx_dates triggers to the two new tables?
Can we confirm idx_hrv_predictions_tiebreak and the partial indexes in sql/audit_re_2026_05_26_covering_partial_indexes.sql exist in prod (pg_indexes) after deployment?
Are there any remaining consumers of the legacy pds.daily_health_matrix, and what’s the plan/timeline to deprecate it?
Is removing garmin_daily_summary from the behavioral spine blocked by any downstream consumer or can we safely cut it now?
